What is Machine Learning?
One of the criticism of AI was, a machine is not intelligent if it 
can not learn.
Learning means doing the similar task efficiently next time.
Machine learning is the science of getting computers 
to act without being explicitly programmed.
Learning programs are adaptive.
requires data.

Why?
Learning vs Memorization
Lots of data available.
Can handle voluminous, complex data to give accurate 
results.
To identify pattern from data.

Examples
Friend suggestion on Social Media platforms.
Product/Video recommendation.
Automatic spam filtering

Types of learning
Supervised
Unsupervised
Reinforced
Semi-supervised

Supervised learning
learns from example data and associated outputs are 
already given.
predicts the correct response for unseen examples. 
similar to human learning under the supervision of a 
teacher. 
Ex: Classroom Teaching

Types
Linear Regression
o Assumption: Linear relationship between independent variable 
(x) and dependent variable (y).
y = β0​+β1​x+ϵ
Polynomial Regression
o Assumption: Non-linear relationship between independent 
variable (x) and dependent variable (y).
y = β0​+β1​x+β1​x2+ . . . +βn​xn +ϵ
Multiple Regression
o two or more independent variables and a single dependent variable.
y = β0​+β1​X1+β1​X2+ . . . +βn​Xn +ϵ
